title: The forgetful helper
prompt:
`main` reads a running total into `x19` and a bonus, asks a helper to double the bonus, and adds the result. With `100` and `20` the total should be 140. Run it: it prints 80.

The helper doubles correctly, but it uses `x19` as scratch. AAPCS64 makes `x19` through `x28` callee-saved: any function that changes them must put them back before it returns, because its caller is still counting on them. Scratch work belongs in `x9` through `x15`, which a caller must assume are gone after any `bl`.

Fix the helper so it does its scratch work in a scratch register and leaves `x19` alone.

## what is checked

- the correct total is printed
- the program exits cleanly
- the helper is still called (`bl` present), and `x19` no longer appears in `double_it`
- the same holds for other totals and bonuses you do not see, zero and negative ones among them
starter:
// add a doubled bonus to the running total
define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

define(total_r, x19)

        .data
fmt_in:     .string "%lld %lld"
fmt_out:    .string "total = %lld\n"

        .bss
        .balign 8
total_m:    .skip 8
bonus_m:    .skip 8

        .text

// double_it(x0 = n) -> x0 = 2 * n
        .balign 4
        .global double_it
double_it:
        mov     x19, x0                     // scratch copy
        add     x19, x19, x19
        mov     x0, x19
        ret

        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, -16]!
        mov     fp, sp

        ldr     x0, =fmt_in                 // read the total and the bonus
        ldr     x1, =total_m
        ldr     x2, =bonus_m
        bl      scanf
        ldr     x9, =total_m
        ldr     total_r, [x9]
        ldr     x9, =bonus_m
        ldr     x0, [x9]                    // the bonus goes to the helper

        bl      double_it                   // x0 = the doubled bonus
        add     total_r, total_r, x0

        ldr     x0, =fmt_out
        mov     x1, total_r
        bl      printf

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], 16
        ret
